pairs.locus: Martin of Braga, Pro repellenda iactantia 5
pairs.question: Si illos qui in bonis operibus viventes humanam gloriam aucupantur auctoritas divina condemnat, eo quod se in illis magis voluerunt laudari quam Deum, quid de illis fiet qui et male vivunt, sed tamen laudari volunt?
pairs.derivation: Author poses a rhetorical question and answers it tersely. Dropped the leading framing 'sed' to start the interrogative; kept the full conditional setup ('Si illos... quam Deum') so 'illis' has a referent. The genuine answer is the curt dismissal 'Ipsi considerent.' which directly responds; stopped there before the next sentence ('Nullus igitur vanae gloriae finis est...') which begins a new point.

pairs.locus: Martin of Braga, Pro repellenda iactantia 7
pairs.question: Ergo nihil caritati, nihil misericordiae, nihil postremo quod gessimus cuicumque deputabitur bonitati?
pairs.answer: Nihil, quia soli inanitati suae vana gloria vindicat quidquid non bonitatis, sed eius imperio est perfectum.
pairs.derivation: An interlocutor's objection posed as a genuine question, answered directly by the author. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'Sed dicit mihi aliquis:' before the question and 'Audacter dicam:' before the answer. Answer ends at the first full stop after 'perfectum'; what follows ('Multa sunt quae de hac contagione dicantur...') turns to transition and is omitted.
